title: Answer-quality evaluation pre-registered: owner-written answer requirements as the yardstick, three methods (chain vocabulary, per-facet rerank, deeper screening) and their pass gates
notes: Owner approved 7 Nov. Joint decision of a three-round literature panel (Astra high, Argon high, Opus high); text notes/2026-11-06-answer-quality/lit-synthesis.md, sha256 28173ac43872359ccbe842a7b1c39e369062e9596653ed20a32cc34c1e35bb3a. Yardstick: 30 new owner-written questions, 3-4 answer requirements each, written before any arm runs and hashed before the arms freeze; the implementing agent never reads them; the six development questions and their topics are excluded; EE test stays a separate reference guard. Methods in build order: M1 chain-admission normalisation plus frozen synonyms and the code-query phrase-collapse fix; M2 rerank-3-lite per concept block plus whole question, interleaved into the top 50, D106 holds kept; M3 single-pass screening of ranks 51-150, K 20, full-text queue by screening grade. Each against one fresh D106 baseline; a combination is its own arm; fused order and 1:1 fused+rerank RRF are diagnostics only. Paired bootstrap over questions, 95%; all gates of a method must pass; inconclusive fails; no retuning, a re-run only for a recorded bug fix. Gates M1: EE pool recall lower bound > 0; median extra chained records <= 80 per run; no code-query clause over 250k works; recall@50 lower bound > -2 pts on BioASQ and LitSearch, > -1.5 on EE; Stage A coverage@50 lower bound > -2. M2: Stage A requirement coverage@50 >= +8 pts with lower bound > 0; precision@50 (grade >= 2) lower bound > -3; same recall guards; Stage B answer-input coverage lower bound > 0 before deployment; own decision row (block phrases go to Voyage). M3: Stage B answer-input coverage >= +10 pts with lower bound > 0; precision among selected K lower bound > -3; screening calls <= 2x; Standard deadline kept; own decision row. No deployment on Stage A alone. Not shown by a pass: general answer quality beyond these 30 questions.

title: A Claude Code step has three turns available, so the CLI can ask the model again when its structured answer does not match the schema, and a session that still ends without a valid answer goes to DEIXIS's own validation instead of pausing as an isolation violation
notes: notes/2026-11-06-answer-quality/pilot3/runs/superseded/{A,B}-battery_soh-r1-attempt1.json: with the claude connection and sonnet, both arms paused with model_isolation_violation, error "Reached maximum number of turns (1)", tool_item_types ["StructuredOutput"]; other questions passed. Cause, read in claude_agent_sdk 0.2.152 and the Claude Code 2.1.316 CLI: output_format is sent as --json-schema and the answer arrives through the CLI's internal StructuredOutput tool, which checks it with Ajv and, on a mismatch, returns the error to the model for another try (bounded by the CLI's MAX_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_RETRIES); with max_turns 1 that retry turn ended the session with error_max_turns and no structured_output, and the adapter counted the StructuredOutput call as an outside tool. Now: max_turns 3 (claude.MAX_TURNS), so up to two further turns are available; built-in tools, MCP servers, skills, setting sources and permission mode dontAsk are unchanged (a later turn may still hold text or thinking instead of a StructuredOutput call). Content blocks of the assistant and user messages the SDK parses are checked: text, thinking, the model's StructuredOutput calls and the results of those calls pass (user-message text is not kept as the answer); any other block there (another tool call, a StructuredOutput call inside a user message, a server tool use such as web_search, a server tool result, a result for an unknown call, an unknown block type) is reported as a tool action and fails the step as model_isolation_violation, whether the session ends in success, at the turn limit, on a timeout or on an SDK error. Other SDK message types (system, stream and task events) are not inspected. A session that ends as error_max_turns or error_max_structured_output_retries with no assistant-level error (such as billing_error), no API error status, at least one StructuredOutput call and no other tool action returns its last StructuredOutput input as the answer text; any API error keeps its service-failure classification. That text goes through the step's usual normalisation, identity stamping and validation: if it then passes, it is accepted without another call; if not, the step's bounded repair runs as for any invalid output (an unverified draft or invalid_model_output when repairs run out). The CLI's verdict (subtype, error, attempts, turns) is stored with the validation record as transport.structured_output. The run's model-call budget counts one call per session, so the extra turns inside a session (at most two) are not counted; each repair gets its own three turns. No fallback model or provider. Sol high review round 1 (notes/2026-11-06-answer-quality/review-d157-sol.md): not ready, four findings fixed; round 2 (review-d157-r2-sol.md): user-message tool blocks were not checked, fixed. Not measured live.

title: The lookup before the rerank sends Crossref 8 requests at once, and a work without an abstract keeps its place for an unfinished lookup only when a request for it went out and its latest answer did not come back
notes: notes/2026-11-06-answer-quality/pilot2/RESULT.md: the 8 s prerank round still hit its ceiling in 4 of 6 D155 runs (Crossref's single requests are slow without a contact email), and D155's unsettled counted every asked record no source answered, including those whose Crossref request was never sent, so 33-69 works without an abstract per run kept their fused place as no_abstract_lookup_open. Owner-approved, for new runs only. (1) inspection.prerank_lookup version 4: crossref_in_flight 8 (was 4); max_requests unchanged at 418, one request per record either way. Each prerank lookup request (Semantic Scholar batch, Crossref single, Scopus group) adds the records it is for to sent and out on its run_steps output once httpcore reports that request's own headers written to an open connection (send_request_headers.complete trace event of the lookup request, matched by method and host so a proxy's CONNECT does not count; hooked through providers.common.on_send; a wait at a pacer, a start gate or for a connection marks nothing, a cooldown-skipped Semantic Scholar batch is not sent, and a transport that emits no trace event marks nothing, so its records count as never sent); its response headers (receive_response_headers.complete) or its stored answer take them off out, so a 429 waiting for its retry is not out, and the next attempt or a retry after a resume puts them back; a step cut short at the ceiling keeps that output. The prerank step stores lookup_open instead of unsettled: asked records still without an abstract that are on some source's out in this round and have no found or not_found from that source in any run. (2) rerank_list reads lookup_open when the stored prerank output has it, else unsettled; the rerank rule (version 3), its reason codes no_abstract_text_route and no_abstract_lookup_open and the held counts in its event are unchanged, so a record with a route to text is held as in D155 and a record no request of the round was sent for, without such a route, is scored on its title. Budgets frozen with version 3 keep D155's unsettled and 4 in flight. Not measured live.

title: Semantic Scholar no longer blocks the other lookups, a work without an abstract keeps its place only when text can still reach it, abstracts come before closest works' further pages, and the extra block-terms semantic request is off
notes: Round 4 of notes/2026-11-06-answer-quality/r4-synthesis.md (Sol high and Argon high agreed). (1) inspection.prerank_lookup version 3: Semantic Scholar waits for no 429 before the rerank (s2_waits 0), one batch of 400 ids (s2_batch), and s2_cooldown_skip: a Semantic Scholar 429 anywhere in the process sets a cooldown on its pacer (15 s, or Retry-After up to 60 s; a retrying caller holds it for its whole wait), set while the refused attempt still holds the pacer gate, its deadline under a lock of its own (the later one always stands); while it lasts the prerank and read-stage lookups of such a run send no Semantic Scholar batch, even one already queued for the gate (it returns at once, not counted as sent), store each of its records failed as after a refused batch (so Quick reaches abstract_not_found as after a real 429), store skipped s2_cooldown with the count on the step and its step_finished event, and go on to Crossref and Scopus; the pacer gap is 3 s (was 2 s); the prerank step stores unsettled: asked records still without an abstract for which some in-scope source either never stored its plan (time ran out first) or listed the record and wrote no answer for it this round (its request was cut short); a failed or cooldown-skipped answer of this round counts as that source's say. Pacer gap and cooldown wait are process-wide, so they also time older runs' requests; nothing else changes for them. (2) inspection.rerank version 3, hold_without_abstract with_text_route: a window record still without an abstract keeps its fused place only with an open PDF URL on a version of its work, a person's upload or a stored file (no_abstract_text_route), or an unsettled lookup (no_abstract_lookup_open); otherwise it is scored on its title as before D153. The rerank's step_finished event and the transcript's rerank line give the held counts by reason; the activity log shows the cooldown skip. fast_path policy admission_order unresolved_last: K admission takes unresolved works after candidates, the person's works first. (3) answer allocation version 6: one abstract per abstract-only work before closest works' pages 2-4; the D152 zero-part closest work gives at most 2 passages. (4) New search plans freeze block_semantic as off (block_terms_off_v2) and send no block-terms semantic request; a plan frozen under D154 still sends it; synonyms, 8-term queries, backups and 4 count probes in flight stay. Budgets frozen before this keep D153's, D152's or older rules. Not measured; offline replay and an ablation come next.

title: Synonyms reach the search: the model's query may hold 8 terms with each block's common synonym or abbreviation, a backup is used when a term finds nothing with the other block, the counts run four at a time, and one more OpenAlex semantic request is sent with the block terms
notes: Combined order step 2 of notes/2026-11-06-answer-quality/r2-synthesis.md. Method text search-query.md: at most 8 terms in total and 4 per block (was 6 in total), each block asked for the common synonym, variant or abbreviation of its main term; this changes skill_package_hash. SearchQuery schema maxItems 4 per block, semantic cap SEARCH_QUERY_MAX_TERMS 8; a person's saved plan follows the same 8; kill-search and follow-up queries keep 6. search_query.check: a kept term whose count with the other block is 0 brings the next unused backup of its block beside it when that backup finds records with the other block and the query stays within 8 terms; the term stays with its warning; a tried backup that does not qualify is stored dropped (zero_results or no_records_with_other_block); each used backup's meta says why (used_because); counts read before a backup was added are read again; MAX_COUNT_REQUESTS 40 (was 24). Count probes in search_query.check and vocabulary.build_vocabulary run 4 in flight (vocabulary.PROBES_IN_FLIGHT); the same queries are asked and the check rows keep their order, but the probe record now lists every chosen term's count before any zero-hit replacement's, so its order differs from before around zero-hit replacements. Sent to OpenAlex: one new semantic request text, the searched setting and task phrases joined, page size semantic_top, after the question's request; frozen in the search plan as block_semantic (rule block_terms_v1, step search:fast:semantic:blocks), skipped with its reason when no block term is searched or the text equals the question's; a plan frozen without block_semantic sends none. No manageable-total guard applies to the model's query (MANAGEABLE_TOTAL narrows only the code query). The plan's word record gains `semantic`, and the transcript and plan panel show a word no keyword query carried but the block request sent apart from words not searched. Backlog (Sol review item 5): the per-block limit was tightened under the same deixis.search_query.v2 identifier; a versioned contract with explicit historical handling is not done (stored answers are not revalidated). The plan screens say a block-semantic word is part of the planned semantic search, not that it was sent. Sol high code rounds: 1 ready with fixes, 2 ready. Pilot 6 Nov with D152+D153 (notes/2026-11-06-answer-quality/pilot/RESULT.md, 4 held-out questions, 1 run per arm): fail, answer-input reference coverage 27.1% before vs 23.2% after, top-50 references 13 vs 16; within one-run noise, no gain shown.

title: A question not in English and without key terms is translated by a model into one English sentence, and the run searches its words instead of pausing for key terms
notes: A new required model step, question_translation, on the literature model with the one schema repair. Sent: the question text and its language hint plus the common StepInput fields (no candidates, sources or passages). The sentence must read as English (code check) and is stored as the revision's English sentence with origin model, written once per revision and never copied to a later revision (a person's sentence still goes with an unchanged question); a sentence the person saved first, or wrote in the revision form, is used and no model is asked, and a resumed or later run reads the stored sentence back with the model its step recorded. Code picks the search words from the sentence; every other model step still reads the question as written. OpenAlex's semantic request and the built-in embedding model now read the sentence too, where before they had none for such a question. A failed or invalid translation pauses the run with key_terms_needed and the reason. Library schema 17 widens the origin list. Translation quality and its effect on search are not measured.

title: A search request answered with a server error (5xx) is sent once more after 2 seconds; a phase that needs attention in a run still at work no longer reads "Stopped while …"
notes: Before, a 5xx counted as delivery unknown and was never resent in the run, so one OpenAlex 503 dropped the whole semantic request. A search is a read, so the resend changes nothing at the provider; it counts against the query allowance and the run like any attempt, and a stop or the stage cutoff during the wait keeps the failed reply. Retry is skipped when the query has no allowance left.

title: arXiv source route: a name only KaTeX knows (\Set), defined once by \newcommand at the top level of the preamble, is trusted like any user macro
